subject.title: feat(workspace): add tiered bootstrap loading with configurable bootstrapTier

question: Should OpenClaw accept `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` as a core config surface now, and should this PR's `minimal`/`standard`/`full` and hook-extra semantics be the accepted contract?
rationale: The code path is bounded and the proof is useful, but adding a public bootstrap config knob changes session context behavior and overlaps existing bootstrap/context controls, which automation should not decide.

options.title: Sponsor This PR Shape
options.body: Proceed with this PR after public docs are added, the branch is refreshed against current main, and maintainers explicitly accept the no-override compatibility and hook-extra tier semantics.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Bootstrap Selection
options.body: Pause this PR and design one broader bootstrap selection contract that covers tiering, per-session filtering, lightweight context, and related prompt-pressure issues together.

options.title: Decline The New Config Knob
options.body: Close this direction and steer users toward existing `contextInjection`, bootstrap budgets, lightweight context mode, and hook configuration instead of adding `bootstrapTier`.

recommendation.title: Sponsor This PR Shape
recommendation.body: Proceed with this PR after public docs are added, the branch is refreshed against current main, and maintainers explicitly accept the no-override compatibility and hook-extra tier semantics.
